title: Krill
objective: After this level you can explain why tiny krill matter so much.
summary: Antarctic krill, about 5 cm long, may have the largest biomass of any wild animal species. They feed penguins, whales and fish, and their young winter under the sea ice.

cards.headline: An animal about 5 cm long may be the heaviest wild species on Earth.
cards.body: Not one of them, of course. All of them together. Meet Antarctic krill, and find out why so much of the Southern Ocean runs on them.

cards.fact: Antarctic krill may have the largest total biomass of any wild animal species.
cards.context: The best estimate for all of them together is about 379 million tonnes. Each one is a small, see-through, shrimp-like crustacean about 5 cm long, and they live in vast, dense swarms. Tiny, but never alone.

cards.headline: Everybody's lunch
cards.body: Krill graze on microscopic algae, and they are the main food for many of the Southern Ocean's bigger animals: penguins, whales and fish. That makes them the link between the smallest living things and the biggest. The blue whale, the largest animal known to have lived, eats almost nothing but krill, up to 6 tons of them a day. The giant runs on the tiny.

cards.headline: A nursery under the ice
cards.body: Winter is the hard part. Young krill spend it under the sea ice, where the rough, complex underside of the ice gives them shelter from predators and access to food. Scientists call winter sea ice the krill's nursery and feeding ground. Remember Level 72's ice that grows every winter? For a young krill, that's the roof over its head.

questions.prompt: Scientists' best estimate of the total weight of all Antarctic krill is about how much?

options.label: About 379 tonnes
options.rationale: Far too small for trillions of animals.

options.label: About 379 thousand tonnes
options.rationale: Still about a thousand times too small.

options.label: About 379 billion tonnes
options.rationale: About a thousand times too big.

questions.explanation: The best estimate for Antarctic krill is about 379 million tonnes, possibly the largest biomass of any wild animal species.

questions.prompt: Why do so many of the Southern Ocean's larger animals depend on krill?

options.label: Krill clean the water so other animals can see
options.rationale: Krill matter as food, not as cleaners.

options.label: Krill keep the ocean from freezing
options.rationale: Krill don't change the water's temperature.

options.label: Krill build the sea ice that animals rest on
options.rationale: Sea ice is frozen seawater; krill live under it.

options.label: Krill are their main food, linking them to tiny algae

questions.explanation: Krill eat microscopic algae and are the main food for penguins, whales and fish, linking the smallest life to the largest.

questions.prompt: Level 63 called estuaries the nurseries of the sea. Where is the nursery for young Antarctic krill?

options.label: In warm tropical lagoons
options.rationale: Krill spend winter in the Antarctic, under the ice.

options.label: Inside river estuaries
options.rationale: Those are Level 63's nurseries; krill use the ice.

options.label: On the open deep-sea floor
options.rationale: They shelter under the ice, close to food.

questions.explanation: Young krill spend winter under the sea ice, whose rough underside gives them shelter from predators and access to food.
